title: Ares Deep
setting: Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.
rules: Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

locations.desc: Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required.

factions.name: Mission Control
factions.desc: The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
factions.stance: supportive but anxious; reviewing this rotation's data for the renewal decision

factions.name: Halvorsen Aerospace
factions.desc: The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.
factions.stance: publicly upbeat; privately watching costs and crew performance

clocks.name: Dust storm arrival
clocks.fireText: The dust storm arrives. The sky turns the color of rust, solar output collapses and anyone outside has minutes to get in.

fireWorld.power: solar output collapsed, running on battery reserve

then.name: Storm clears
then.fireText: The storm finally breaks. Weak sunlight returns, and the solar field sits under a thick blanket of dust.

fireWorld.power: solar arrays recovering; panels caked with dust

then.name: Battery reserve depleted
then.fireText: The battery reserve hits critical. Non-essential systems shut down, and life support switches to rationing.

fireWorld.power: critical: battery nearly drained, life support only

clocks.name: Water recycler failure
clocks.fireText: The water recycler grinds to a halt. Until it is repaired, the station is on stored water only.

then.name: Stored water runs low
then.fireText: Stored water drops below the safety margin. Every liter now has to be argued over.

facts: An orbital weather relay shows a regional dust storm building east of Hellas and tracking toward Ares Deep, roughly twenty hours out.
opening:
The coffee substitute tastes like hot cardboard, same as every morning. What isn't the same is the sound: the water recycler in hydroponics has picked up a dry, unhealthy rattle that carries all the way into the commons.

Okafor sits at the galley table with her tablet, reading the overnight weather relay. "Dust storm building east of us," she says without looking up. "Twenty hours, maybe less. I want the arrays secured and the Mule inside by tonight."

Teo hovers by the galley counter, eyes on the recycler readout, unusually quiet. Somewhere down the corridor the lab door has been sealed since before you woke; that's Lev. Then the intercom crackles: Priya, from the garage, asking whether anyone has signed off on the Mule's battery swap yet, because she is not doing it twice.

It's going to be a long sol.
